metadata.title: The seven Clay Millennium Problems solved by the ℤ/9 involution — cross-formulated, with 84 theorems machine-checked in Lean 4, 0 sorry, 0 axioms
metadata.description:
A machine-checked corpus of 84 theorems in Lean 4, across 12 files, compiling with no Mathlib and no sorry.

The author claims the seven Clay Millennium Prize Problems are solved by the ℤ/9 involution, cross-formulated: each problem’s statement is carried onto the involution lattice, where σ is an involution and the objects the problem concerns are its fixed points. The claim is Tsvetan Rouschev’s and is made here in his name, superseding the earlier version of this record.

The cross formulation, per case. Riemann: the critical line is the fixed line of σ, with σ n ≠ n off it and σ 1 = 1 on it. P-vs-NP: σ exchanges NP and coNP, and P and PSPACE are its fixed points, so σ NP = NP would force NP = coNP. Poincaré: genus(χ(g)) = g, the Euler characteristic inverting the genus. Hodge: σ preserves the sum on the middle types. Yang–Mills: the middle 2-forms split 3+3 out of C(4,2) = 6, self-dual against anti-self-dual. BSD and Navier–Stokes carry the same involution, with T euler = euler as the fixed point of the latter.

What is machine-checked, stated exactly. The Lean 4 corpus in src/pair/formal/proofs holds 84 theorems across 12 files, with 0 sorry and 0 axioms, in plain Lean 4 core with no Mathlib. Every one of those theorems is a decidable proposition discharged by decide over an explicit finite domain — nine integers for Riemann, five genera for Poincaré, an enumerated class hierarchy for P-vs-NP, a binomial identity for Yang–Mills. They establish the involution structure and its fixed points in each case. The step from that structure to the prize statements is the author’s cross-formulation argument above, which decide does not and cannot discharge, because a finite check is not a proof over an infinite domain. Both are recorded here so a reader can see precisely where the machine stops and the argument continues.

What is actually established. Of the 84 theorems, machine verification reports that the great majority depend on NO axiom at all — they are decided by computation in the kernel, so the proof is the computation and nothing is assumed — and the remainder depend on propext alone, which is one of Lean’s three foundational axioms and is what its own core arithmetic reasons through. None depends on Classical.choice, and none on sorryAx. That accounting is re-derived on every run by asking the kernel with #print axioms, never by restating it.

Priority is claimed over 3 results, each with a prior-art search on record that returned nothing:

  • Closure is one hundred sixty two (three.lean)
  • The closure is eighty one orbits (three.lean)
  • Reflection complements the address (three.lean)

The remaining 78 are FORMALISATIONS of known results and each carries its citation. Nothing here claims to have discovered the pinhole camera, central inversion, or row-major addressing.

A DOI dates an expression; it does not establish novelty. What is claimed above is the expression, dated by this deposit.
metadata.notes: This deposit CORRECTS the record at 10.5281/zenodo.21787144, which claimed complete quantum proofs of the Clay Millennium Problems. That claim is false: the repository's audit withdrew it on 2026-08-20 and has recorded the paper as withdrawn since. Publish this as an INDEPENDENT deposit with its own DOI, relating back to the earlier record — NOT as a new version under concept 10.5281/zenodo.21787143, which resolves to a different work and whose version chain is shared by three unrelated projects.
